title: Asteroids
summary: State-local variables on a timed mode, an HSM in-game parent whose pause handler the three children inherit, and push$/pop$ pause where the pop target genuinely varies.
teaches: State-local variables ($.timer) · HSM-inherited pause · push$/pop$ where the pop target varies across $Playing / $ShipDying / $WaveClear
controls: ←/→ turn · ↑ thrust · SPACE fire · H hyperspace · P pause

machines.title: AsteroidsGame — push$/pop$ pause where pop target varies
machines.blurb: Top-level controller, parameterized by a starting difficulty. Attract zeroes the game, then start advances into the $InGame parent which holds Playing (the rally), ShipDying (the brief stun after the ship explodes), and WaveClear (between waves). Because pause() is handled on the $InGame parent, every child inherits it — push$ stashes whichever child was active and transitions to Paused; resume pops back to that exact child. Three callers, three possible pop targets — this is where the state stack actually earns its weight.

machines.title: Ship — state-local variables for a timed mode
machines.blurb: The ship's modes: Alive (steerable, can shoot, can be hit), InHyperspace (the 0.4s blink-out — invulnerable, invisible), Exploding (the death animation), Respawning (a brief grace window after respawn), Dead (out of lives). $InHyperspace is the showcase: $.timer and $.duration are STATE variables — they belong to that compartment only and are created fresh on every entry, so each hyperspace begins with $.timer = 0 without any reset logic. The transition out is a plain → $Alive (no push$/pop$) because $Alive is the only caller; the state stack only earns its keep when there are multiple.
